look_here_first: Cream-white ELONGATED flower SPIKES (rather than round heads of S. roemeriana), distinctive hooked prickles on woody twigs and notably broader/longer leaflets than most Gregg's catclaw. For Gregg versus Wright, measure several mature leaflets and check whether the inflorescence is comparatively loose and whether ripe pods curl.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Thorny shrub or small tree, locally sometimes tree-sized.

key_traits.label: Armature
key_traits.text: Short hooked recurved internodal prickles on stems, not paired stipular spines.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Bipinnate, often 1–4 pinna pairs and 3–6 leaflet pairs per pinna. Leaflets obovate. The 2024 regional key gives about 5–9(-12) mm long, but its own species description gives 3–6 × 2–3 mm; numeric overlap/inconsistency warrants measuring several fully mature leaves, not a single strict cutoff.

key_traits.label: Flowers
key_traits.text: Cream to yellowish-white flower SPIKES, elongated rather than spherical, often more open/less compact than Gregg's.

key_traits.label: Pods
key_traits.text: Broad, flat pods, often slightly constricted; can be distorted or coiled, so curvature alone not definitive.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Larger round-obovate leaflets than typical Gregg's catclaw

key_traits.label: Petiole gland
key_traits.text: A capitate gland is reported at/near the proximal pinna pair; requires a verified tight macro before adding a training arrow.

key_traits.label: Pod confirmation
key_traits.text: Usually straight-to-slightly curved in regional key, but detailed 2024 treatment also permits coiled pods. Do not exclude Wright based only on a curled pod.
